told_more: The record tells me when each thing happened, why, and how the houses were kept; the views are plain clay-coloured with no paint, wear, signs or people, so they show only the changes to the shape of a house: A's shopfront there until 2010 and gone by 2020, B's bakery front (2000) and balcony (2010), the boards coming off D (2010) and going onto E (2010), the trim on C's windows (2000 and 2020), and D's lean-to. Everything about upkeep, use (ironmonger, cafe, bakery, empty), repaints, 1965/1971 window swaps and E's neglect from 1993 is invisible in them. The views did help me see where the houses stand and how a change reads on the street (D on its rock, E closing the lane), so they add the look, but they tell me less about what happened.

contradicts.claim: House A has a bay window (with brackets) on the upper-left corner of its quay-road front in every year, 1989 to 2020; the record gives A no addition at all and lists no bay.
House B in 2010 and 2020 has a glazed, enclosed ground-floor extension under the balcony over the lane (a glazed side bay with tall panes); the record mentions only a balcony.

B's bakery front (2000, 2010, 2020) looks like blank closed panels, not a glazed shop window like A's; it reads as shut or boarded and not as a bakery in trade, and it does not change when A's shop (record: closed 2009) closes.
In the city view B's roof looks like a low-pitched ribbed roof, and not clearly flat as the record says (1936 functionalist, flat roof); from eye level it is hidden behind a straight parapet edge.

The record says C's 2011 back windows are factory 'old style' replacements after the 1998 restoration copies; in the 2020 views they look more framed and traditional than the plain 1971 ones and about as good as the 1998 copies, so they read as an improvement, not a cheap change.

views_showed: Which changes can be seen at all, and at what distance: shopfronts and the balcony read at eye level and 12 m; boards on D and E read clearly at 12 m and street level; window trim on C shows only close up; at city scale almost nothing reads except B's balcony and shopfront and faint boards.

D and E swap places over the years: D (on the rock) goes from boarded in 1989 and 2000 to open and glazed in 2010 and 2020, while E at the top of the lane goes from open in 1989 and 2000 to boarded in 2010 and 2020, so the lane's end view turns from lived-in to shut.
A's roof and upper floor stay the same in all four years while only the shopfront changes, and by 2020 A reads as a plain house again with ordinary windows at street level.
B's balcony sits over the lane on top of a glazed ground-floor bay, which the record does not make obvious; and A has an upper bay window the record does not list.

C's 1998 restoration shows only as trimmed window frames at the upper gable; the 2011 change shows as a differently glazed window at the back, so a viewer can see 'something was changed' but cannot tell 'copies of the originals' from 'factory old-style' windows.
D's lean-to at the back is visible in all years, including 1989, so it reads as old rather than new.
missing: Repaints and paint age (A 1949/1996/2016, B 1987/2003/2017, C 1998/2013, D 2007), so the kept or neglected state of a house cannot be seen, A's 40 years without paint in 1989 included.
Use and trade: the ironmonger, the cafe and its move, the bakery, the closing of A's shop in 2009 (the shopfront looks the same in 2000 and 2010), and signs or names.

Neglect that is not boarding: E empty from 1993 (E looks the same in 1989 and 2000), D's leaking roof in 1995, E 'still empty' in 2015 (2010 and 2020 look identical), and any weathering or damage on roofs.
The 1965 front windows on D and E and the cheap 1971 windows on C (nothing shows them as replaced).

The burning down of B in 1935 and its rebuild in 1936 (only the final functionalist form is seen, so a viewer cannot tell the house was rebuilt), and the original 1912, 1884, 1879, 1828 and 1826 builders and their causes.
All causes and people: owners, heirs, the break-in, the city's rules for the wooden town, whether a house is lived in, and any activity on the street (no people in any view).
